section.content: The present invention provides a kind of semiconductor integrated circuit, in NAND cell type EEPROM, executes write-in data input action parallel in data write activity so that shorten the time required to entire data write sequence.Wherein, with after action by success/failure result of the action be held in chip the 1st action and the 2nd action, when the 1st action and the 2nd action are carried out continuously, there is the action of success/failure result output after the 1st and the 2nd acts both the 1st action and the 2nd action.
本发明提供种半导体集成电路，在NAND单元型EEPROM中，在数据写入动作中并行执行写入数据输入动作，使得整个数据写入顺序所需时间缩短。其中，具有在动作结束后在将该动作的成功/失败结果保持于芯片内的第1动作及第2动作，在第1动作和第2动作连续进行时，具有在第1和第2动作结束后把第1动作和第2动作这两者的成功/失败结果输出的动作。

Semiconductor integrated circuit having a plurality of transistorsThe present application is a divisional application of an invention patent application having an application number of 201010543237.6, a divisional filing date of 2010, 11/15/and an invention name of "semiconductor integrated circuit" (an original parent application having an application number of 02157191.0, an application date of 2002, 12/19/and an invention name of "semiconductor integrated circuit").

Technical Field

The present invention particularly relates to a semiconductor integrated circuit that outputs success/failure results of internal operations to the outside of a semiconductor chip, AND more particularly to a nonvolatile semiconductor memory device such as a NAND cell EEPROM, a DINOR cell EEPROM, AND an AND cell EEPROM.

Background

As one of semiconductor memory devices, an electrically rewritable EEPROM is known. In particular, a NAND cell type EEPROM in which a plurality of memory cells are connected in series to form a NAND cell block has attracted attention as a device capable of high integration.

One memory cell of the NAND cell type EEPROM has a FET-MOS structure in which a floating gate serving as a charge storage layer and a control gate are stacked via an insulating film on a semiconductor substrate. Then, a plurality of memory cells are connected in series so that adjacent memory cells share a source and a drain to form a NAND cell, and this NAND cell is connected to a bit line as a unit.

Such NAND cells are arranged in a matrix form to constitute a memory cell array. The memory cell array is integrated in the p-type well region or the p-type substrate. The drains of one end side of the NAND cells arranged in the column direction of the memory cell array are commonly connected to a bit line through selection gate (gating circuit) transistors, respectively, and the source of the other end side is connected to a common source line through another selection gate transistor.

The control gate of the memory cell transistor and the gate of the select gate transistor extend in the row direction of the memory cell array, and are respectively a common control gate line (word line) and a common select gate line.

The operation of this NAND cell type EEPROM is as follows.

The data write operation is performed sequentially from the memory cell located farthest from the bit line contact. A high voltage Vpgm (about 18V) is applied to the control gate of the selected memory cell. From this selected memory cell, an intermediate potential Vmw (about 10V) is applied to the control gate and the select gate of the memory cell located on the bit line contact side, and 0V or an intermediate potential Vmb (about 8V) is applied to the bit line in accordance with data.

When the bit line potential is 0V, the potential is transmitted to the drain of the selected memory cell, and electron injection occurs by a tunnel current from the drain to the floating gate. Thereby, the threshold of the selected memory cell is shifted in the positive direction. This state is taken as, for example, a "0" write state.

When the bit line potential is Vmb, electron injection does not occur, and therefore, the threshold value does not change, and stops at a negative value. This state is a "1" write state.

Data erase is performed simultaneously for all memory cells in the selected NAND cell block. That is, 0V is applied to all control gates in a selected NAND cell block, and a high voltage Vera (about 20V) is applied to the p-type well region or the p-type substrate. In addition, the bit lines, the source lines, the control gates in the non-selected NAND cell blocks, and all the select gates are made to be in a floating state.

Thus, in selecting all the memory cells in the NAND cell block, electrons of the floating gate are discharged to the p-type well region or the p-type substrate due to the tunnel current. Thereby, the threshold voltage shifts in the negative direction after the erasure.

In the data read operation, 0V is applied to the control gate of the selected memory cell, and a power supply voltage Vcc or a read voltage VH slightly higher than the power supply voltage is applied to the control gates and the select gates of the other memory cells. The value of voltage VH is generally a voltage level 2 times or less Vcc, for example, 5V or less. At this time, data can be read by detecting whether or not a current flows in the selected memory cell.

Fig. 35 shows an example of a configuration of a memory cell array and a bit line control circuit of a conventional NAND cell type EEPROM.

Fig. 35 shows an example in which the memory cell array 1 has bit lines BL0 to BL33791 and 1024 blocks Block0 to Block1023 of 33792, for example, and row decoders are arranged on both sides in the row direction.

In the bit line control circuit 2, a detection latch circuit 31 is provided between a data input/output buffer memory and a transmission/reception data path IO,/IO line pair and bit lines BLi, BLi + 1. (i ═ 0). That is, one detection latch circuit 31 is connected between each IO,/IO line pair and 2 bit lines of adjacent odd and even columns.

Fig. 36 shows an algorithm of an example of a data writing procedure of the NAND cell type EEPROM of fig. 35.

In this algorithm, data is sequentially written to each of a plurality of pages. In the data write operation, the detection latch circuit 31 is in operation, that is, in use, the detection latch circuit 31 cannot be used for other operations such as data input.

That is, in this data writing sequence, the write data input operation and the data writing operation are executed for 1 page, and the data writing operation is repeatedly executed for each page, so that the write data input operation cannot be executed in parallel in the data writing operation.

In the actual operation, after the data writing operation is completed, the written data is read, and a write check is performed to determine whether the written data matches the data to be written, and to confirm whether the normal writing is completed.

Therefore, in the data writing sequence, the write data input operation and the data write operation are alternately repeated. The time required for the entire data writing sequence is mainly the sum of the time required for processing the write data input operation and the time required for processing the data writing operation, and the time required for the entire data writing sequence becomes long.

Fig. 37 shows an algorithm of an example of the reading sequence of the NAND cell type EEPROM in fig. 35.

This algorithm shows the sequence of the case where data is read out successively for each of a plurality of pages. In the data reading operation, since the detection latch circuit 31 is in operation, that is, in use, the detection latch circuit 31 cannot be used for other operations such as data output.

In the algorithm of fig. 37, the time required for the entire data read sequence is increased by the time required for both the cell data read operation and the read data output operation and the time required for determining the entire read sequence.

Further, in order to realize a cache function and a multi-value logic operation, a memory circuit including a data writing/reading circuit for temporarily holding write data and read data is provided, and as for such a circuit, for example, patent document 1 is disclosed, and japanese patent laid-open No. 2001-325796 is disclosed.

Disclosure of Invention

As described above, in the conventional nonvolatile semiconductor memory device such as the NAND cell type, there is a problem that the write data input operation cannot be executed in parallel in the data write operation, and the time required for the entire data write sequence becomes long.

In addition, there is a problem that the read data output operation cannot be executed in parallel in the data read operation, and the time required for the entire data read sequence becomes long.

The present invention has been made in view of the above problems, and a first object of the present invention is to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit capable of outputting success/failure results of both operations to the outside and improving the convenience of control outside a chip when the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation, which hold the success/failure results of the operations in the chip after the operations are completed, are continuously performed.

It is a second object of the present invention to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit which can realize a semiconductor memory circuit having a high-speed data writing function by inputting write data in parallel in a data writing operation and shortening the time required for the entire data writing sequence.

It is a third object of the present invention to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit which can output read data in parallel in a data reading operation, shorten the time required for the entire data reading sequence, and realize a semiconductor memory circuit having a high-speed data reading function.

The semiconductor integrated circuit of the first invention aspect is characterized in that: the method includes continuously performing a1 st operation and a2 nd operation, internally holding a success/failure result of the 1 st operation after the 1 st operation is completed, and externally outputting both the success/failure result of the 1 st operation and the success/failure result of the 2 nd operation after the 1 st and the 2 nd operations are completed.

The semiconductor integrated circuit of the second inventive aspect is characterized in that: the 1 st action and the 2 nd action can be executed in parallel, and both the 1 st information indicating whether the 1 st action is being executed and the 2 nd information indicating whether the 2 nd action can be executed in the 1 st action are output to the outside.

A semiconductor integrated circuit according to a third aspect of the present invention includes: an internal circuit that can perform acts 1 and 2 in parallel; and an output circuit for outputting to the outside both 1 st information indicating whether the 1 st action is being executed and 2 nd information indicating whether the 2 nd action can be executed in the 1 st action.

A semiconductor integrated circuit according to a fourth aspect of the present invention includes: a success/failure determination circuit for determining the result of the internal circuit which has just operated and outputting a success/failure signal; a success/failure holding circuit for receiving the success/failure signal and holding the success/failure results of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation, which are continuously executed, in the internal circuit; and an output circuit that outputs a success/failure result of each of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation held by the success/failure holding circuit when the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation are continuously performed.

A semiconductor integrated circuit according to a fifth aspect of the present invention includes: a data cache circuit connected to the data input/output line and temporarily holding data; and a latch circuit connected to the data cache circuit, for reading and latching data read from the memory cell, and latching data to be written into the memory cell.

Detailed Description

Embodiments of the present invention will be described below with reference to the drawings.

< embodiment 1>

Fig. 1 is a block diagram showing an overall schematic configuration of a NAND cell type EEPROM according to embodiment 1 of the present invention.

In the memory cell array 1, as will be described later, a plurality of memory cells each having a control gate and a select gate are provided. A bit line and a word line are connected to each of these memory cells. The plurality of memory cells are divided into a plurality of blocks, and one of the blocks is selected during operation.

A bit line control circuit 2 is connected to the memory cell array 1. The bit line control circuit 2 reads data from a plurality of memories in the memory cell array 1 and writes the data into each memory cell.

Therefore, the bit line control circuit 2 includes a sense amplifier for detecting and amplifying the potential of the bit line in the memory cell array 1 and a sense latch circuit (sense amplifier/data latch circuit) for latching data for writing. Then, data transfer such as write data and read data is performed between the bit line control circuit 2 and the data input/output control circuit 3.

The data input/output control circuit 3 includes a data cache circuit for holding write data, read data, and the like, and controls input/output of internal data or external data such as write data and read data, as will be described later. The data input/output control circuit 3 is connected to a data input/output buffer (I/O buffer) 4.

The data input/output control circuit 3 is controlled by the output of a column decoder 6 that receives an address signal from an address buffer (address latch) 5 that receives an address input.

A row decoder 7 for controlling the control gates and select gates of the memory cells is connected to the memory cell array 1. Further, a well potential control circuit 8 for controlling the potential of a p-type well region or a p-type substrate forming the memory cell array 1 is connected to the memory cell array 1. In addition, a source line control circuit 9 for controlling a source line voltage within the memory cell array 1 is connected to the memory cell array 1.

Further, a word line control circuit 10 for controlling the potential of the word line, that is, the gate line in the selection block, and a row decoder power supply control circuit 11 for controlling the power supply potential of the row decoder 7 are provided. The word line control circuit 10 and the decoder power supply control circuit 11 are connected together to the row decoder 7.

Further, a high voltage and intermediate voltage generating circuit 12 is provided which generates a high voltage and intermediate voltage for writing, a high voltage for erasing, a high voltage for reading, and the like, supplies the high voltage and intermediate voltage to the p-type well region or the p-type substrate in the erasing operation, and supplies the high voltage and intermediate voltage to the word line and the bit line in the memory cell array 1, the row decoder 7, and the like in the writing operation. The high voltage and intermediate voltage generation circuit 12 is connected to the memory cell array 1, the bit line control circuit 2, the word line control circuit 10, and the decoder power supply control circuit 11.

The data input/output buffer 4 transmits and receives various data to and from the outside. To this data input/output buffer 4, for example, 8I/O pads composed of I/O-1 to I/O-8 are connected. Then, write data, addresses, commands, and the like are supplied from the outside through the 8I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8, and read data and various signals are internally output to the outside through the 8I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8.

The data input/output buffer 4 is also connected to the address buffer 5 and the command decoder 13.

When a command is inputted from I/O-1 to I/O-8, the command decoder 13 receives the command through the data input/output buffer 4, latches the command, and outputs a control signal for controlling various operations such as a data read operation, a write operation, and an erase operation in accordance with the latched command.

In addition, a success/failure determination circuit 14 and a success/failure holding circuit 15 are provided. The success/failure determination circuit 14 is connected to the bit line control circuit 2, and the success/failure holding circuit 15 is connected to the success/failure determination circuit 14. The success/failure holding circuit 15 is constituted by, for example, a shift register.

The success/failure determination circuit 14 determines whether or not writing or erasing is performed normally. Then, if writing or erasing is normally performed, it is determined as a pass state, and if not, it is determined as a fail state.

The success/failure determination by the success/failure determination circuit 14 is transmitted to the success/failure holding circuit 15 for holding after the end of the write or erase operation. Then, a command for checking the success/failure state is supplied from the outside through the I/O-1 to I/O-8, the command is input to the command decoder 13 through the data input/output buffer 4, a control signal is output from the command decoder 13, the success/failure determination result held in the success/failure holding circuit 15 is input to the data input/output buffer 4 in accordance with the control signal, and then, any one of the I/O-1 to I/O-8 is selectively output.

In addition, a "ready"/"busy" control circuit (R/B control circuit) 16 is provided. The R/B control circuit 16 is connected to the data input/output control circuit 3 and the data input/output buffer 4. The ready/busy control circuit 16 generates a ready/busy signal indicating an operation state of the chip in accordance with the operation of the data input/output control circuit 3. This ready/busy signal is input to the data input/output buffer 4, and then selectively output from any one of the I/O-1 to I/O-8.

Fig. 2(a) and (B) are a cross-sectional view taken out of a NAND cell portion in the memory cell array of fig. 1 and an equivalent circuit diagram, and fig. 3(a) and (B) are a cross-sectional view taken along line 3A-3A and a cross-sectional view taken along line 3B-3B in fig. 2(a), respectively.

A memory cell array composed of a plurality of NAND cells is formed on a p-type silicon substrate (or p-type well region) 22 surrounded by an element separation oxide film 21. In one NAND cell, a plurality of memory cells (in this example, 8 memory cells M1 to M8) connected in series share the n-type diffusion layer 23 (23) serving as the source and drain regions of each of the adjacent cells0、 231、...、2310)。

Further, on the drain side of the NAND cell, there are provided gate transistors 24 formed simultaneously with the floating gate control gates of the memory cells, respectively9、259And 2410、2510。

Each of the memory cells M1-M8 has a structure in the form of a gate insulating film 26 on the semiconductor substrate 22To form a floating gate 24 (24)1、242、...、248) And a stacked control gate 25 (25) is formed thereon via a gate insulating film 271、252、...、258)。

The substrate on which the element is formed is covered with a CVD oxide film 28, and a bit line 29 is arranged thereon. Bit line 29, and diffusion layer 23 on the drain side of one end of the NAND cell0Are in contact.

The NAND cells are arranged in a matrix, and the gate transistors on the drain side of the NAND cells are commonly connected to a source line, and the gate transistors on the source side are connected to the source line (source line voltage cell-source).

The control gates 24 of the memory cells M1 to M8 are arranged in the row direction of the memory cell array as control gate lines (word lines) CG1, CG 2.

Fig. 4 is a diagram showing a part of an equivalent circuit of the memory cell array 1 in fig. 1 in which NAND cells shown in fig. 2(a) and (b) are arranged in a matrix.

A NAND cell group sharing the same word line and select gate line is called a block, and for example, a region surrounded by a dotted line in the drawing is one block. The operations such as read/write are performed for one selected block selected from the plurality of blocks.

Fig. 5 is a circuit diagram showing an example of the configuration of the memory cell array 1, the bit line control circuit 2, and the data input/output control circuit 3 in fig. 1.

As shown in fig. 5, the IO/IO line pair, which is a path for transmitting and receiving data to and from the data input/output buffer 4, is connected to a plurality of sense latch circuits 32 provided in the bit line control circuit 2 via a plurality of data cache circuits 31 provided in the data input/output control circuit 3. Each of the data cache circuits 31 and each of the sense latch circuits 32 includes 2 inverter circuits whose input and output nodes are cross-connected to each other. More specifically, each data cache circuit 31 is configured to include: a latch circuit 33 including 2 inverter circuits, a switching transistor 34 connected between one data storage node N1 of the latch circuit 33 and an IO line, a switching transistor 35 connected between the other data storage node N2 of the latch circuit 33 and a detection latch circuit 32, and a switching transistor 36 connected between the data storage node N2 and the detection latch circuit 32.

Each detection latch circuit 32 includes a latch circuit 37 including 2 inverter circuits, and a switching transistor 38 having one end connected to the data storage node N3 of the latch circuit 37. In the bit line control circuit 2, 2 switching transistors 39 and 40 are provided for each of the detection latch circuits 32. The one transistor 39 is connected between the other end of the transistor 38 and any one bit line in the even column in the memory cell array 1, and the other transistor 40 is connected between the other end of the transistor 38 and any one bit line in the odd column in the memory cell array 1. The transistors 39 and 40 are gated by a bit line selection signal BTL0 or BTL 1.

That is, the IO,/IO line pair is directly connected only to the data cache circuit 31, and the data cache circuit 31 is connected to the sense latch circuit 32.

Fig. 5 shows an example in which the memory cell array 1 has 33792 bit lines BL0 to BL33791 and 1024 blocks, that is, blocks 0 to 1023 (blocks 0 to 1023), and row decoders are arranged on both sides in the row direction.

In the circuit of fig. 5, there are 2 kinds of latch circuits, i.e., 1 detection latch circuit 32 and 1 data cache circuit 31, between 2 bit lines of odd columns, even columns and IO,/IO line pairs. Therefore, in the data write operation and the data read operation, only 1 of the 2 bit lines connected to the sense latch circuit 32 is selected, and data write/read can be performed only on the memory cell connected to the selected bit line.

Since only the detection latch circuit 32 is used in the data write operation, the data cache circuit 31 can be used in an operation independent of the data write operation. For example, the write data used in the data write operation to be performed below, that is, the input operation of the write data to be written to the next page may be used.

Fig. 6 is a diagram showing an algorithm of an example of a data writing sequence in the case of using the circuit of fig. 5.

This algorithm shows a case where a data write operation and a write data input operation to write data to a next page are performed in parallel in a data write sequence in which data is written to each page of a plurality of pages in sequence. In the first step, a write data input operation (to the data cache) to the data cache circuit 31 is performed, and in the next step, an operation (using the detection latch) of transferring the write data from the data cache circuit 31 to the detection latch circuit 32 is performed from the data cache circuit 31. In addition, this data write operation is performed in parallel with an operation of inputting the next write data to the data cache circuit 31 (to the data cache).

In the same manner, data is transferred from the data cache circuit 31 to the detection latch circuit 32, and a data write operation is performed.

In the algorithm of fig. 6, a data transfer operation from the data cache circuit 31 to the detection latch circuit 32 is necessary. However, since the time required for the normal data transfer operation is very short, typically about 2 to 3 μ s, compared with the data write operation (typically about 200 μ s) and the write data input operation (typically several tens to several hundreds of μ s), the time required for the entire sequence is hardly affected.

Next, the advantage of the algorithm of fig. 6 over the algorithm of fig. 36 shown in the conventional example will be described by comparing the time required for the data write operation for 1 page.

The time required for the data write operation for 1 page by the algorithm of fig. 6 is the sum of the time required for the data write operation and the time required for the write data transfer operation, which is longer than the time required for the data write operation and the write data input operation performed in parallel therewith. In contrast, the time required for the data write operation for 1 page by the algorithm shown in fig. 36 in the conventional example is the sum of the time required for the data write operation and the write data input operation.

Considering that, generally, the time required for the data write operation is as long as about 200 μ s, and the time required for the write data input operation is several tens to several hundreds of μ s, since the data write operation and the write data input operation are of the same order of magnitude, when the algorithm of fig. 6 is used, the time required for the 1-page write data input operation is about several hundreds of μ s.

In contrast, the time required for the data write operation for 1 page using the algorithm of fig. 36 is several hundred μ s + several hundred μ s, and the time required for the entire sequence using the algorithm of fig. 6 can be significantly shortened.

Fig. 7(a) to (f) are diagrams schematically showing the operation of the circuit of fig. 5 when the algorithm of fig. 6 is used.

In fig. 7, the data write operation performed in parallel with the write data input operation is denoted by "Background", and the individual operation of the data write operation is denoted by "Foreground". The Data writing operation is represented as "Data programming" (Data Prog), and is performed by repeating a voltage applying operation "programming" (programming) and a write verifying operation "verifying" (verifying) for writing Data into the memory cell.

In the data write operation of the last page in the data write sequence, since the write data of the next page must be input, fig. 6 and 7 together become a single operation of the data write operation. Therefore, the background operation is not necessary for the data write operation to the final page. That is, because there is no need to act in parallel with other actions, foreground actions may be used.

Fig. 8 is a diagram illustrating an example of a method of controlling a data writing sequence of a semiconductor chip formed of the NAND cell type EEPROM of fig. 1. The operations in the periods Ta to Tf in fig. 8 correspond to (a) to (f) in fig. 7.

As a control method for realizing the write operation, generally, there are adopted an address/data input command (COM1) input, an address input for performing data writing, a write data input, an input of a data write operation start command, and a start of a data write operation in this order, and there are two types of data write operation start commands: a command COM2 for foreground, i.e. data write action that can be performed in parallel with the write data input action, and a command COM3 for background, i.e. data write action that cannot be performed in parallel with other actions.

When the command COM3 for one data write operation is input, the busy period of the ready/busy state indicating the operation state of the chip is long, and the busy state continues until the data write operation ends in accordance with the input of the command COM 3. In this "ready"/"busy" state, the operation of the data input/output control circuit 3 in fig. 1 is detected in the R/B control circuit 17, and a "ready" signal/"busy" signal is generated in response to this detection state.

When the command COM2 for the other data write operation is input, the "busy" period of the "ready"/"busy" state indicating the operation state of the chip is short, and the write data input immediately before the command COM2 is input is returned from the "busy" state to the "ready" signal/"busy" state immediately after the write data is transferred from the data cache circuit 31 to the detection latch circuit 32.

In general, by using the command COM2 in addition to the final page in the data writing order as the data writing operation start command, the data writing operation and the write data input operation can be executed in parallel to shorten the required time, and the end of the order can be easily detected by using the command COM3 for the final page. That is, it is particularly effective to adopt a method that can be detected by checking the ready/busy state.

In addition, the respective required times shown in fig. 8 correspond to 2112 bytes for 1 page as the input data amount, the data input cycle is 50ns, the time required for data transfer from the data cache circuit 31 to the detection latch circuit 32 is 3 μ s, the time required for data write operation is 200 μ s, and the data write sequence shown is from page 1 to page N.

In the method shown in fig. 8, a "busy" state is output in a simulated manner during the execution of the background write operation, for example, during Tc and Td. In this simulated "busy" state, the input of commands other than commands associated with the write operation, such as COM1, COM2, and COM3, particularly commands associated with other operations, for example, a data read operation and a data erase operation, is prohibited. The input of the inhibition command is generally described in the specification of the chip.

In addition, the chip is designed in such a way that when the prohibition command is input, the prohibition command can be ignored to continue the background operation, and the malfunction can be prevented.

Specifically, the valid command, the disable command, or the negligible command can be exemplified as follows. The valid command is a write series command such as COM1, COM2, COM3, or the like, a reset command, a command that outputs a signal indicating a ready/busy state and a success/failure state. The inhibit command or the negligible command is a command other than the above-mentioned valid command, for example, a read series command, a delete series command.

The valid command and the disable command do not have any problem, such as a chip ID output command, but these are generally included in the disable command, and have an advantage that a circuit can be simplified.

In general, when the success/failure state is examined after a certain operation is completed, a chip state output command COMS is input to I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8. The chip status output commands COMS inputted from the I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8 are supplied to the command decoder 13 via the data input/output buffer 4 in fig. 1, where control signals for outputting success/failure statuses are generated.

On the other hand, as described above, after the data write operation is completed, the success/failure state of whether or not the write operation has been completed normally is held in the success/failure holding circuit 15. To investigate this success/failure status, a chip status output command COMS is input in I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8. Accordingly, the data held in the success/failure holding circuit 15 is output to the I/O pads I/O-1 to I/O-8 through the data input/output buffer 4.

Generally, an operation of outputting a state of a chip state including a success/failure state after a chip state output command COMS is input is called a state read.

In actual operation, there are many cases where data of several pages to several tens of pages are written continuously, and in this case, an accumulated state is output in which the success/failure of the writing operation of several pages to several tens of pages is accumulated.

For this accumulation state, there is a manner in which resetting can be performed by a normal reset command, and there is a manner in which resetting can be performed by a dedicated reset command using only the accumulation state.

If there is a state of success/failure accumulation from the immediately after-reset action to the last action as the accumulation state, there is also a state of success/failure accumulation only for a certain specific action or command, for example, a write action and a write-series command.

That is, in the NAND cell type EEPROM in embodiment 1, when the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation, in which success/failure results of the operations are held in the chip after the operations are completed, are continuously performed, the success/failure results of both operations can be outputted to the outside of the semiconductor chip, and convenience in control outside the chip can be improved.

In addition, the NAND cell type EEPROM can perform the 1 st action, for example, data write action, and the 2 nd action, for example, write data input action in parallel, and has an action of outputting both data indicating whether the 1 st action is being performed, for example, true-R/B, and data indicating whether the 2 nd action can be performed in the 1 st action, for example, cache-R/B, to the outside of the semiconductor chip.

Therefore, the write data input operation can be performed in parallel in the data write operation. Accordingly, the time required for the entire data writing sequence is determined by whichever of the time required for the write data input operation and the time required for the data writing operation is longer, and the time required for the shorter one does not affect the sequence required time. Therefore, the time required for the entire data writing sequence can be shortened, and a high-speed data writing function can be realized.

Further, as described above, it is preferable to basically have the following configuration requirements in order to realize the operation of holding the success/failure result of the operation in the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation in the on-chip state after the end of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation in the semiconductor integrated circuit, and to output both the success/failure result of the 1 st operation and the success/failure result of the 2 nd operation to the outside of the semiconductor chip after the end of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation when the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation are continuously performed.

That is, the constitution preferably includes: a success/failure determination circuit (success/failure determination circuit 14) that determines the result of an operation to be performed by the integrated circuit internal circuit and generates a success/failure signal; a success/failure holding circuit (success/failure holding circuit 15) for receiving the success/failure signal and holding the respective success/failure results of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation performed continuously by the integrated circuit internal circuit; and an output circuit (data input/output buffer 4) for outputting the success/failure results of the 2 operations held in the success/failure holding circuit to the outside of the semiconductor chip when the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation are continuously performed.

Further, by providing an accumulation result holding circuit for accumulating and holding the success/failure results of the 1 st operation and the 2 nd operation in succession, the accumulation result of the 2 operations held in the accumulation result holding circuit and/or the success/failure results of the 2 operations held in the success/failure holding circuit are outputted from the output circuit to the outside of the semiconductor chip.

Fig. 25 is a diagram schematically showing an algorithm of a data read procedure in a case where the present invention is applied to the data read operation of the circuit of fig. 5.

Here, when data is read out successively from a plurality of pages, the unit data read-out operation and the read data output operation are executed in parallel.

In this way, since the cell data read operation and the data output operation for the following page 2 are executed in parallel, the time required for the entire sequence is determined by the time required for the longer operation of the cell data read operation and the data output operation, and the time required for the shorter operation is not affected.

That is, in each operation of fig. 24, the read data transfer time is about 2 to 3 μ s, the cell data read operation time is about 25 to 50 μ s, the read data output operation time is about 25 to 100 μ s, and the read data transfer time is extremely short compared to other operations. Therefore, the time required for the data read sequence is governed by the cell data read operation and the read data output operation.

In contrast, in the algorithm of the above-described conventional example shown in fig. 37, the total sequence time is determined by the sum of the cell data read operation time and the read data output operation time. Therefore, one of the algorithms in fig. 24 can realize a higher data reading sequence than the algorithm of the conventional example shown in fig. 37.

Valid and prohibited commands in the background operation (cache-R/B is in the ready state, true-R/B is in the busy state) during data read, or the following commands can be ignored. That is, the valid command is a read series command such as COM6, COM7, COM8, COM9, or a reset command, and a command which outputs signals indicating a ready/busy state and a success/failure state. The inhibit command or the negligible command is a command other than the valid command, for example, a write series command, a delete series command, or the like.

There are cases where there is no problem with either of the valid command and the disable command, such as a command for outputting a chip ID, but these are generally included in the disable command, and there is an advantage that a circuit can be simplified.

In the operation of fig. 29(b), when data of the final page is read, since there is no sub-page, even if the read-series command COM6 is continuously input, the data read operation is sufficient for the final page at one time.

Therefore, when the read-series command COM6 is continuously input to the final page, the data read operation is omitted from the input of the 2 nd and subsequent commands COM6, and the output of the "busy" state is performed only for a short time, for example, about 2 to 3 μ s, or only the read data transfer operation may be performed. In this case, since the data read operation is omitted, the operation time, i.e., the "busy" period can be shortened.

Further, the write data input operation can be performed in parallel in the data write operation, and the time required for the entire data write sequence can be shortened, thereby realizing a semiconductor memory device having a high-speed data write function.
